summary: Well‑documented, artifact‑backed preregistered paired evaluation that honestly reports a deterministic ceiling caused by two preregistered design choices (shared_initial_generation and reuse of the same deterministic validator as both runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer). Execution and analysis artifacts are comprehensive and internally consistent; the manuscript correctly interprets the ceiling as a design outcome rather than evidence about verifier utility in general. The study’s main value is methodological: a concrete, artifact‑grounded diagnosis and actionable benchmark‑hardening recommendations for future confirmatory runs.
required_revisions: Add an aggregated difficulty-summary (counts and percentages per difficulty level: medium/hard/very_hard) computed from the archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl and include it in the manuscript (Results or Appendix) so the claim of benchmark diversity is supported by in‑paper, artifact‑derived numbers.

Replace the current generic reference to an 'archived verified bibliography' in the References section with explicit full bibliographic entries for the key prior works cited in Related Work (use the verified citation records already archived in the artifact bundle). The paper must contain standard in‑manuscript references for nearest prior work rather than pointing readers solely to the artifact archive.

Move or add one concise sentence in Methods (and mirror in the Abstract) that explicitly states, up front, that the preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and reuse of deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as both runtime guard and scorer render the preregistered primary estimand effectively untestable in this execution (i.e., the design produced a deterministic ceiling). This explicit statement must be unambiguous so readers can immediately interpret the confirmatory null as a design consequence rather than a substantive null result.
optional_revisions: Add a small in‑manuscript summary table (1 row) showing execution accounting numbers (planned episodes, completed episodes, model_calls_used, complete_pairs, repairs_applied) drawn from analysis/condition_summary.csv to improve readability; artifacts support this directly.

Briefly (1–2 sentences) clarify the pre‑lock rationale for selecting shared_initial_generation and the single deterministic validator (if that rationale exists in archived pre‑lock notes) or explicitly state that the choice was made to isolate validator acceptance on identical generator outputs; reference the archived preregistration for details.

If space permits, add one representative pair (task ID) as a compact worked example (task manifest entry + validator_trace excerpt) to illustrate how shared candidate acceptance leads to identical outcomes; artifact examples exist for this and can be cited.
